title: Console Watchtower: privilege chronicle and cost-alignment flow
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design and prototype a unified audit and access-explorer UI for the Redwood Console that connects temporal role grants to application-level cost signals and rollout windows. The Watchtower flow helps security and platform teams answer: who had sensitive permissions at a given time? what access changes coincided with cost spikes or deployment rollouts? and can owners attest to access for quarterly compliance?
design_notes: Primary surface: Privilege Chronicle (timeline-first view) that lets users scrub back to any timestamp and see effective role grants across orgs and workspaces.
Secondary surface: Cost Alignment pane that overlays per-workspace token/compute spend and highlights correlated permission changes and model-switch rollouts.
Search & clustering: Event clustering groups permission events by actor, object, and rollout id to reduce noise for long timelines.
Attestation flow: One-click attestation cards for role owners with templated justification and optional bulk-revoke action linked to a canary rollback policy.
Rollout integration: annotate timeline with rollout windows and provide a ‘replay state’ showing API routing/model variants active at that time.
Privacy constraints: anonymize customer identifiers in shared views; default to workspace-level aggregates unless user has elevated audit scope.
Accessibility: keyboard-first timeline scrubbing and ARIA labels for cluster summaries.
Performance: incremental query strategy for long histories (30d+), with an initial summary then progressive fetch for details.
Open questions: acceptable retention window for timeline detail; default sampling cadence for cost overlay (hourly vs. 5m).
